newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mark gains ground, Euro bourses take profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mark gains ground, Euro bourses take profit.

text.p: The mark gained against the dollar and yen in early European trading on Wednesday, while leading stock markets took a cue from Wall Street to take some more profits after a record-breaking streak.
The U.S. and Japanese currencies ceded ground to the mark as the German currency advanced to its highest level in more than 3-1/2 years versus the yen.
Traders said a growing belief in the currency market that Japanese interest rates would stay low for some time was helping to boost the mark.

Reinforcing this belief, Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita said that while the economy was growing gradually, it was unlikely to accelerate soon and market expectations of higher rates were receding.
The mark/yen rate shot through its previous 1996 high of 73.78 in early European business to hit a peak of 74.05 -- its highest since February 1993.

"The mark/yen surge is the by-product of a market that has been very underweight (in) marks on the one hand, while getting constant noises from Japan about maintainence of low interest rates there," said Michael Burke, economist at Citibank.

But U.S. official and corporate comments about the harm which a high dollar rate could have on U.S. competitiveness with Japan jolted the dollar against the yen. It hit a low of 112.04 yen before recovering.
Wall Street fell back overnight on concern about corporate earnings. U.S. bond prices also headed lower after the Treasury sold $18 billion of new notes.
European bourses had taken a slip on the dominant world stock market into account in afternoon trading on Tuesday but Frankfurt in particular lost more ground when trading opened for a new day.
A weaker dollar, unhelpful for exporters, weighed on German share prices.

With little scheduled company news due and investors having lost some of their enthusiasm for a new buying spree, the London stock market edged lower. "It's very thin today. There's very little around," said one London trader.
The FTSE index of leading British shares had fallen nearly 16 points on Tuesday despite the announcement of a major cable merger.
News on Wednesday of slightly weaker than expected British retail sales data, down 0.3 percent in September from August, helped the market to trim earlier losses and bond prices to edge higher.
Pearson shares hit a record high of 752 pence after recent bid speculation and management changes. But by 0920 GMT they were trading 7-1/2 pence lower at 735.
The Paris bourse also started in the minus column, following the dip on Wall Street and weakness in the dollar and bonds.
Shares in resorts group Club Mediterranee, which issued a profits warning late on Tuesday, re-quoted down nearly 16 percent after being suspended limit down at the opening.
CURRENCIES AT 0920 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5250 marks and 112.85 yen, compared with Tuesday's late European levels of 1.5347 and 112.83 yen .
STOCKS AT 0920 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 1.2 points at 4,056.0.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was 20.05 lower at 2,698.93.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 9.59 weaker at 2,166.22.

The Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue-chip shares fell 29.07 points to close at 6,061.80 on Tuesday. Investors sold shares in technology companies after Digital Equipment Corp reported a bigger-than-expected loss.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $383.95 an ounce in the morning, up from $383.65 at the London close on Tuesday. Silver added one cent to $4.98.
